messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate observed on EU routing layer for Dedicated instances. 90th p50 latency spiking, retries increasing. Trigger: routing-service >= 5% 5m error rate. Auto-page: @sre_oncall_maya @sre_oncall_dan.

sre_oncall_maya: I’m on it. joining bridge in 2m. Can someone dump the list of affected enterprise accounts? we need contact routing.

account_ops: Pulling affected customers now — looks like a routing table flap in eu-west-2 impacting dedicated customers with pinned capacity. Preliminary list (ids + owner):
- acct_47f3 (AtlasFin) — julia.csm@atlasfin.com / +44 7700 900111
- acct_9a1b (SolaraHealth) — pm@solarahealth.com / +44 7700 900222
- acct_d2c8 (NimbusRetail) — ops@nimbus.com / +44 7700 900333
- acct_f1e5 (BetaBank) — englead@betabank.com / +44 7700 900444

julia_csm: Adding context — AtlasFin is on an enterprise contract with dedicated networking (VPC peering). They’ve already opened an internal ticket; they’ll expect hourly updates.

mike_infra: Confirming we see gRPC timeouts from the routing mesh to gpu-pool-eu-01. Kernel logs show intermittent socket resets. Dumping relevant logs to the bridge.

sre_oncall_maya: Action plan (first 15m):
1) Confirm scope and map accounts to routing nodes.
2) Failover routing-policy for impacted nodes to eu-west-1 (soft-failover) where capacity exists.
3) Notify affected customers with tailored impact statements.
4) Keep Status Page update + internal exec note.

ops_pager: Paging schedule: I'm handing off to @sre_oncall_dan in 30m for the next 8hr window. Dan — please take over the on-call bridge and customer comm cadence.

sre_oncall_dan: Ack. Will take bridge at 1800 UTC. Please leave a handoff note in the bridge when you pass.

chris_pm: We need to minimize risk of data plane inconsistencies. If we soft-failover, ensure we preserve KV cache affinity for active streams. Mike — can you confirm cache warming plan?

mike_infra: We will replay recent cache prefixes to eu-west-1 and enable prefix-copy mode. It will add ~200ms per hot query for the first 60s. Low risk.

julia_csm: Draft customer notification for enterprise customers (please edit):
"Hello {CustomerName},
We’re investigating an issue affecting inference requests routed through our EU dedicated routing layer. Some requests may see increased latency or transient failures. Our engineers are performing a controlled failover to an alternate EU region to restore throughput. We expect the mitigation to complete within the next 30-45 minutes. There is no evidence of data loss; request retry semantics are in place. We will send another update in 60 minutes or sooner if the status changes. For urgent concerns, contact your designated account lead: {AccountContact}.
— Redwood Inference Incident Team"

sre_oncall_maya: Edit suggestions: call out that dedicated instances might be routed to a different region and token billing unaffected, and include temporary API header that customers can use to force prefer-origin if they want to avoid cross-region routing.

julia_csm: Updated template:
"Hello {CustomerName},
We’re investigating an issue affecting inference requests routed through our EU dedicated routing layer which may cause elevated latency or transient request failures. As a mitigation, we are performing a controlled failover to an alternate EU region; some tenants on Dedicated capacity will see requests served from eu-west-1 instead of eu-west-2. This may increase latency by ~200-500ms for a short window. Token billing behavior is unchanged. No data loss is expected. If you prefer to avoid cross-region routing during mitigation, please set header X-Redwood-Prefer-Origin: eu-west-2 and notify your account lead.
We’ll provide an update within 60 minutes. For urgent inquiries contact {AccountContact}.
— Redwood Inference Incident Team"

account_ops: I’ll send that to AtlasFin and BetaBank now. Using the following routing for notifications: primary email -> pager -> phone.

sre_oncall_maya: Also adding a Status Page public update (short):
"Investigating — We are seeing elevated error rates for requests routed through our EU dedicated routing layer. A controlled failover to an alternate EU region is in progress. Some Dedicated customers may experience increased latency or transient failures. We will post updates every 60 minutes or as conditions change."

sre_oncall_dan: Internal exec note (one-liner for Slack #general-exec):
"Incident: EU Dedicated routing spike — controlled failover to eu-west-1 in progress. Impacting ~4 enterprise Dedicated customers. No data loss reported. Engineering team engaged; updates every 60m."

mike_infra: Quick troubleshooting logs for handoff: paste from routing-service (last 2 mins):
```
[2026-03-15T17:41:02Z] routing-mesh eu-west-2 conn_reset node=rt-eu-03
[2026-03-15T17:41:05Z] grpc timeout  upstream=gpu-pool-eu-01/192.0.2.14 code=14
[2026-03-15T17:41:11Z] socket: ECONNRESET on fd 23
[2026-03-15T17:41:22Z] route-table reload triggered by sync error
```

sre_oncall_maya: Handoff note for @sre_oncall_dan — in bridge: we started controlled failover at 17:43 UTC; eu-west-1 capacity warmed with prefix-copy; customer notifications sent to AtlasFin and BetaBank. Remaining: confirm SolaraHealth & NimbusRetail have been notified, monitor error rate down to <0.5% and latency back to baseline, then revert routing-policy.

sre_oncall_dan: Received. My priorities on takeover:
- Continue monitoring error-rate and tail latencies via dashboard panel "Routing->EU Dedicated"
- Coordinate with Mike for rollback plan if failover causes anomalies
- Keep hourly updates to customers and Slack exec note

julia_csm: Confirmed: SolaraHealth and NimbusRetail have been messaged via email and paged. Solara asked for a 1:1 call; scheduling with their CTO now.

account_ops: Delivery logs: AtlasFin email delivered 17:45 UTC, BetaBank delivered 17:46 UTC, SolaraHealth delivered 17:47 UTC, NimbusRetail delivered 17:48 UTC. All pagers triggered.

sre_oncall_dan: Good. If we hit <0.5% error rate for 10m, we set a tentative revert window of +30m and notify customers about revert timing.

chris_pm: Keep track of billing implications — confirm no double-billing during region shift. Finance has been paged as FYI.

mike_infra: Confirmed: no double charge — backend token accounting uses request id; region change won’t cause duplicate charges. Added a debug flag to audits for this incident: audit_incident_id=INC1799998888.

incident-bot: Incident update (17:55 UTC): mitigation in progress — error rate down to 2.1% (was 5.7%). Customers notified. Next update in ~35 minutes or on major status change.

sre_oncall_dan: Taking over bridge now. Leaving this thread as the canonical handoff log.

julia_csm: Leaving customer follow-up checklist for Dan: 1) quick post-mortem bullet for AtlasFin 2) share revert ETA with customers 3) schedule post-incident postmortem with CS + Eng.

sre_oncall_dan: Acked. Will post a short timeline and root-cause hypotheses in #postmortems once stabilized.

account_ops: Final note: contact routing map for on-call teams during this event:
- Primary: account_ops -> email -> pager -> phone (as above)
- Secondary: julia_csm (customer success) -> direct CSM channel -> account exec
- Escalation: chris_pm -> sales-lead -> legal if contract-impact suspected

sre_oncall_dan: Thanks everyone — handing off command to NOC rotation at 18:30 UTC. Adding incident tag INC1799998888 and closing active pager once error rate <0.5% for 10m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: RESOLVE CONDITIONS: error_rate < 0.5% sustained 10m AND customer revert notices sent.
